name: browser-app-builder
description: Guide a student from local setup to a planned, tested browser app and GitHub Pages publication, with bundled Campus Designer styling.

interface.shortDescription: Plan, build, evaluate, and publish a browser app. No coding experience is required.
interface.longDescription: Turn a problem you understand into a self-contained browser application, with a saved plan, local revision history, calculation evidence, and GitHub Pages publication. Your agent handles the files and commands; you make the product and model decisions. Five workflow skills select from seventeen approved library skills for charts, diagrams, timelines, schedules, tables, React controls, slides, animation, CSV, data transformation, statistics, and reproducible randomness. Library apps use an agent-managed Node/npm/Vite build; simple apps can still use native browser features without Node. Bundled Campus Designer guidance and library-specific themes provide consistent Duke colors and typography. The live examples include independently reviewed library applications and the earlier version 0.1.1 plain-app trials, all using simulated planning conversations and synthetic data. Local mapping, bounded SQL exploration, worker-based optimization and controlled silent-video rendering are approved for the reviewed configurations. Video rendering requires an established license basis and explicit acceptance and disclosure of Remotion render-event telemetry; video content remains local.
defaultPrompt: Use setup-browser-app to prepare this folder.
Use plan-browser-app to help me plan a pricing scenario calculator.
Use build-browser-app to implement the agreed PLAN.md.
Use evaluate-browser-app to check the calculations with me and record the evidence.
Use deploy-browser-app to help me publish the evaluated app on GitHub Pages.
Help me plan an interactive analytical presentation with local pricing scenarios.
Help me plan an editable process diagram.
Help me plan a dashboard that imports a local synthetic CSV.

io.github.jordanmeyer.label: Pilot candidate · Instructor-built
io.github.jordanmeyer.audience: MBA students building a self-contained decision tool, dashboard, or simulation with an agent.

results.label: Passing browser checks across ten reviewed examples
Local video exports independently decoded and reviewed
Earlier plain-app trials published and verified live
New recipe apps independently reviewed and verified live

io.github.jordanmeyer.method: Ten original applications were built from recorded simulated planning conversations on a configured Mac. Persistent independent review produced revisions before each PASS, followed by exact-commit GitHub Pages deployment and live checks. The ten browser suites total 268 passing checks. Reviews caught calculation-test gaps, production filtering, keyboard and focus problems, stale browser-restored controls, narrow layouts, SQL extension autoload and video text validation. Five local video exports were independently decoded and reviewed; a sixth rendered on the live site was downloaded, decoded and played to completion. Download automation exceeded tool timeouts, so reliable unattended download delivery is not claimed. The earlier version 0.1.1 plain-app trials and version 0.2.0 library fixtures remain separate historical evidence. These are maintainer-run simulations, not student outcomes or automatic ChatGPT Work routing trials. Exact prompts, source checkpoints, failed rounds, corrections, reviewer verdicts and deployment records are available in the full evidence record.
io.github.jordanmeyer.limits: Self-contained apps use bundled public/synthetic data or locally selected files. No backends, logins, external runtime APIs, remote AI, analytics, secret keys or remote fonts/scripts. Managed builds require compatible Node/npm and host file, shell and browser capabilities. Library approval covers the recorded versions/configurations, not arbitrary combinations. Work routing, clean-machine macOS/Windows and novice-student usability remain unverified. Browser checks do not certify a business model or full accessibility. Exception: the controlled Remotion video recipe sends disclosed render-event telemetry to Remotion (IP, origin, render type/status; no video content). It requires the app owner’s explicit acceptance and a suitable license basis; approval for the recorded example does not transfer automatically to other apps.
